html.body: Author: Marcio Acencio, Luxembourg Centre for Systens Biomedicine, University of Luxembourg Description: Set of pathways encompassing the replication cycle of SARS-CoV-2: attachment, entry, translation, transcription, replication, assembly and release.

Name: rough endoplasmic reticulum The rough (or granular) endoplasmic reticulum (ER) has ribosomes adhering to the outer surface; the ribosomes are the site of translation of the mRNA for those proteins which are either to be retained within the cisternae (ER-resident proteins), the proteins of the lysosomes, or the proteins destined for export from the cell. Glycoproteins undergo their initial glycosylation within the cisternae.
Name: virion The complete fully infectious extracellular virus particle.

Name: double membrane vesicle viral factory A cytoplasmic viral factory that consists of a double-membrane bound vesicle. Has a diameter of 200-300nm and is derived from the endoplasmic reticulum or Golgi apparatus. Produced by Picornaviridae, Nidovirales, Arteriviridae and Coronaviridae.
Name: cytoplasm All of the contents of a cell excluding the plasma membrane and nucleus, but including other subcellular structures.

Name: endoplasmic reticulum-Golgi intermediate compartment A complex system of membrane-bounded compartments located between endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and the Golgi complex, with a distinctive membrane protein composition; involved in ER-to-Golgi and Golgi-to-ER transport.

Name: translation initiation complex A ribonucleoprotein complex that contains a ribosome, mRNA, and initiator tRNA; the functional ribosome is at the AUG, with the methionyl/formyl-methionyl-tRNA positioned at the P site.
Name: viral nucleocapsid The complete protein-nucleic acid complex that is the packaged form of the genome in a virus particle.
